title: Creating space: why focus means stopping most things so the important ones can win
summary: Jason Cohen argues that "focus" only works if you actually stop doing most things. Each thing you drop (bad-fit customers, generic marketing, minor metrics, parallel opportunities) frees time and energy to execute the few things that decide whether a company thrives or perishes.

principles.text: Only by stopping most things do you get the time and energy to execute the important ones deeply; those decide thriving versus perishing.
principles.quote: Only when we stop doing most things, do we have the time and energy to fully, deeply execute the most important things. And the important things are the difference between thriving and perishing.

principles.text: Stop selling to poor-fit prospects: you gain 3x the pitches, each closing at 3x the rate.
principles.quote: When you stop trying to sell people who aren't a good fit, you create space for 3x more sales pitches, each with 3x the close-rate.

principles.text: Help draining customers leave so you can spend time on easy, happy ones who spend more every year.
principles.quote: When you help draining customers exit the business, you create space to spend time with easy, happy ones, who want to spend more every year while giving you positive energy.

principles.text: Skip the 1% improvements everywhere and put effort into the one biggest thing for a 30% gain.
principles.quote: When you stop trying to improve everything by 1%, you create space to improve the biggest thing by 30%.

principles.text: Stop pleasing ill-fitting customers so satisfied ones become fanatics who drive word of mouth, reviews and retention.
principles.quote: When you stop trying to please every ill-fitting customer, you create space to convert "satisfied" customers into "fanatics" who increase word-of-mouth growth, leave positive reviews, and never cancel even if something bad happens.

principles.text: Don't be novel in everything (UX, code, pricing, org); choose a few truly impactful ways to differentiate.
principles.quote: When you stop trying to do everything in a novel way (UX, coding, pricing, org structure), you create space for a few truly impactful modes of differentiation.
